issues.claim: AquaCikl reports discharge limits of 0.10 mg/L manganese and 0.30 mg/L iron. These are reported limits, not independently verified legal acceptance criteria; the applicable sampling point and analytical definitions still require confirmation.

sources.quote: Serbian regulation SR-IED-2023 lowered the allowable manganese in treated discharge to 0.10 mg/L and iron to 0.30 mg/L.

issues.explanation: Jev rates the support of this claim by its quoted evidence at 0.37; restate it to match the quote or remove it.

issues.claim: Žigić’s manganese jar tests used synthetic water and pre-oxidation before coagulation. Her continuous-flow iron–manganese study also identified a tradeoff: at low Fe/Mn ratios, competition reduced iron removal by 12 percentage points. Manganese improvement therefore cannot substitute for checking iron.

sources.quote: Jar-test experiments were performed on synthetic water containing 0.5–4.0 mg/L dissolved Mn(II)
Pre-oxidation with KMnO₄ at stoichiometric doses converted Mn(II) to colloidal MnO₂ prior to coagulation.
At low Fe/Mn ratios (1:1), competition for coagulant capacity reduced Fe removal by 12 percentage points.

issues.explanation: Jev rates the support of this claim by its quoted evidence at 0.42; restate it to match the quote or remove it.
